samples.summary: applyCellStyle can call tree.styleByPath with an empty attribute map on a clear-only edit; the sibling applyCellSpan guards the identical call
samples.evidence: After the new clear path deletes the cleared key from `merged` (line 2444), `attrs = serializeCellStyle({...cell, style: merged})` can be `{}` for a cell whose only serialized attribute was `backgroundColor` (a cell parsed back from the tree gets `padding` only if the attr exists — parseCellStyle ~line 276 — and colSpan/rowSpan are skipped when unset). Line 2457 then calls `tree.styleByPath(cellPath, {})` unconditionally, whereas applyCellSpan at line 2507 deliberately wraps the same call in `if (Object.keys(attrsToSet).length > 0)`. Depending on the SDK, an empty style op is at best a wasted CRDT operation broadcast to peers and at worst throws inside doc.update, aborting the transaction so the removeStyleByPath on line 2461 never runs and the background is never cleared.

samples.summary: MemDocStore leaves the cleared cell-style key present with value undefined, diverging from the Yorkie store it claims parity with
samples.evidence: `cell.style = { ...cell.style, ...normalizeCellStyleClears(style) }` spreads a patch whose `backgroundColor` is explicitly `undefined`, so the key stays present on the cell style object (`'backgroundColor' in cell.style === true`). The adjacent comment claims this "keeps this cache in step with the Yorkie store, which removes the attribute outright", but YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2444) `delete`s the key from `merged`, so the two stores produce structurally different cell styles for the same user action. Any consumer using key presence rather than truthiness (structural style equality, Object.keys diffing, snapshot comparison) behaves differently in local vs collaborative mode.
searchedFor: grep cell.style / style.backgroundColor consumers in docs+frontend src

finding.summary: Table-cell "None" still passes `backgroundColor: ""` and is NOT covered by the new normalization — in the Yorkie path the old color survives in the CRDT
finding.evidence: The fix normalizes `''` only for `InlineStyle` (`normalizeStyleClears` is wired into `applyInlineStyle` and `applyStyleInTree`). The cell-style picker at docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230 calls `editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" })`, which flows through `Doc.applyCellStyle` → `YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2410). There `merged = {...cell.style, backgroundColor: ''}` and `serializeCellStyle` (line 239: `if (s.backgroundColor) attrs.backgroundColor = ...`) drops the falsy value, so `tree.styleByPath(..., attrs)` — a merge-only op with no `removeStyleByPath` counterpart — leaves the previous `backgroundColor` attribute on the cell node. The local cache is then set to `''` (line 2434), so the cell looks cleared locally while peers and any reload still read the old fill: cache/CRDT divergence and a silently lost user action. This is exactly the #793 class of bug the change set out to fix, left in place on one of the call sites the accompanying lessons note counts (docs/tasks/active/20260817-docs-highlight-none-clear-lessons.md:13).

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. `YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle` IS covered by the new normalization and DOES have the removal counterpart the finding says is missing: yorkie-doc-store.ts:2437 calls `normalizeCellStyleClears(style)` (mapping `backgroundColor: ''` -> explicit `undefined` via types.ts:269/271-283/307-309), line 2443-2444 computes `removedCellStyleAttrs(clearedStyle)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:260-264, matching keys present-with-undefined) and deletes them from `merged`, and lines 2458-2462 issue `tree.removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, removeAttrs)` right after `tree.styleByPath` — so the old `backgroundColor` attribute is removed from the CRDT node, not left behind. The cache assignment at 2466 uses that same `merged` object, so there is no cache/CRDT divergence. The MemDocStore counterpart is normalized too (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:287). An existing test re-reads through a fresh `YorkieDocStore` to bypass the optimistic cache and asserts `'backgroundColor' in reread.style === false` while `verticalAlign` survives (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2060-2074). The finding's cited line numbers (2410, 2434) also do not correspond to `applyCellStyle` in the current file (2410 is inside `updateTableCell`).
